title: Avoid loading the user in GET /users/<id>/posts
bug: Unknown users get an empty list instead of 404.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The diff removes the User existence check (db.session.get(User, id) or abort(404)) and directly queries posts by user_id, causing requests for non-existent users to return 200 with empty data instead of 404, which the PR description does not announce as intended.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The diff removes the User existence check (db.session.get(User, id) or abort(404)) and directly queries posts by user_id, causing requests for non-existent users to return 200 with empty data instead of 404, which the PR description does not announce as intended.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The diff removes the User existence check (db.session.get(User, id) or abort(404)) and directly queries posts by user_id, causing requests for non-existent users to return 200 with empty data instead of 404, which the PR description does not announce as intended.

doppel_guided.summary: The PR removes the 404 response for non-existent users in GET /users/<id>/posts, changing it to 200 with empty results, which is an unannounced regression.

suspicions.claim: GET /users/<id>/posts no longer returns 404 when the user does not exist; it returns 200 with an empty list.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/users/999999/posts with a valid Bearer token. Read back status code and response body. Expect 200 and {'data': [], 'pagination': {...}} instead of 404.
suspicions.evidence: Probe 'probe_s1_empty_user' sent GET /api/users/999999/posts; base returned 404, head returned 200 with empty data and pagination.

suspicions.claim: The @other_responses({404: 'User not found'}) decorator remains on the endpoint but the 404 is never raised, so API documentation incorrectly advertises a 404 response.
suspicions.trigger: Inspect the generated API docs at /docs (or /apifairy/spec) for the GET /users/<id>/posts operation and verify that a 404 response is still documented.
suspicions.evidence: Probe 'round2 probe_s2_doc_404' fetched /docs but the response shows only title and empty arrays, so it cannot be determined whether the 404 response remains documented.

suspicions.claim: Pagination metadata (total, offset, limit, count) for a non-existent user incorrectly reports total=0 instead of a 404 error.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/users/999999/posts?limit=10 with a valid Bearer token. Read back rv.json['pagination']['total'] and rv.json['data']. Expect total=0 and data=[] with status 200.
suspicions.evidence: Probe 'probe_s3_pagination_total0' sent GET /api/users/999999/posts?limit=10; base returned 404, head returned 200 with pagination total=0 and empty data.

suspicions.claim: Posts belonging to a deleted user (user_id references a non-existent user) are now returned by this endpoint, whereas before they were excluded because the user load failed.
suspicions.trigger: 1) Create a user and a post. 2) Delete the user directly in the DB (bypassing cascade). 3) Send GET /api/users/<deleted_id>/posts with a valid Bearer token. Read back status and data. Expect 200 with the orphaned post in data; previously this would have been 404.
suspicions.evidence: Probes for s4 created a post and attempted to delete the user via DELETE /api/me and DELETE /api/users/me, both returning 405 Method Not Allowed, so the user was never deleted and the orphaned-post scenario was not reached.
